content.content_text: The 98th Academy Awards ceremony took place on March 15, 2026, at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, with Conan O'Brien hosting for the second year in a row. One Battle After Another (2025) was the big winner of the night, with six awards, including Best Picture, Best Director and Best Adapted Screenplay for Paul Thomas Anderson, as well as the first Oscar for Best Casting, presented to Cassandra Kulukundis. Sinners (2025) broke the all-time record for nominations, with 16, and won four, including Best Actor for Michael B. Jordan, the second actor to win for playing two roles in the same film. Brazil once again competed for Best Picture and Best International Feature Film with The Secret Agent (2025), by Kleber Mendonça Filho, which also earned Wagner Moura a Best Actor nomination.

content.title: Records and trivia
content.description: Autumn Durald Arkapaw, of Sinners (2025), became the first woman to win the Oscar for Best Cinematography. Best Live Action Short Film ended in a tie between The Singers (2026) and Deux personnes échangeant de la salive (Two People Exchanging Saliva, 2025), the first Oscar tie since 2013. Amy Madigan earned her nomination for Weapons (2025) 40 years after her first, for Twice in a Lifetime (1985), the longest gap between nominations for an actress. Sean Penn did not attend the ceremony, and the Best Supporting Actor award was accepted on his behalf by Kieran Culkin.

content.content_text: The 97th Academy Awards ceremony took place on March 2, 2025, at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, hosted for the first time by comedian Conan O'Brien. Anora (2024) won five awards, including Best Picture, and Sean Baker became the first person to take home four Oscars in the same night for a single film (picture, director, original screenplay and film editing). I'm Still Here (2024), by Walter Salles, gave Brazil its first win in the Best International Feature Film category and was also the first Portuguese-language film nominated for Best Picture; Fernanda Torres was nominated for Best Actress.

content.title: Records of the night
content.description: Emilia Pérez (2024) arrived at the ceremony with 13 nominations, the most ever received by a non-English-language film. Adrien Brody gave the longest acceptance speech in Oscar history, at 5 minutes and 37 seconds. Straume (Flow, 2024) was the first independent animated film to win Best Animated Feature and gave Latvia its first Oscar, and Paul Tazewell, of Wicked (2024), was the first Black man to win the award for Best Costume Design.

content.content_text: The 96th Academy Awards ceremony took place on March 10, 2024, at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, hosted by Jimmy Kimmel for the fourth time. Oppenheimer (2023), by Christopher Nolan, was the big winner, with seven awards, including Best Picture, Director, Actor (Cillian Murphy) and Supporting Actor (Robert Downey Jr.). Poor Things (2023) won four statuettes, including Best Actress for Emma Stone, and The Zone of Interest (2023) took home two.

content.title: Records
content.description: The Zone of Interest (2023), winner of Best Sound, and Godzilla Minus One (2023), winner of Best Visual Effects, were the first non-English-language films to win in those categories. Lily Gladstone became the first Native American nominated for Best Actress, and Billie Eilish, who won Best Original Song for "What Was I Made For?", became the youngest person to win two Oscars.

content.content_text: The 94th Academy Awards ceremony took place on March 27, 2022, at the Dolby Theatre in Hollywood, hosted by Regina Hall, Amy Schumer and Wanda Sykes. CODA (2021) won Best Picture and was the first winner in the category released by a streaming platform, while Dune (2021) was the most awarded film of the night, with six statuettes. Troy Kotsur became the first deaf man to win an acting Oscar, and Jane Campion became the third woman to win Best Director, for The Power of the Dog (2021).

content.title: The slap
content.description: During the presentation of the Best Documentary Feature award, Will Smith walked onstage and slapped comedian Chris Rock after a joke about his wife, Jada Pinkett Smith. About forty minutes later, Smith won the Oscar for Best Actor for King Richard (2021). Days later, he resigned from the Academy, which banned him from attending its events, including the Oscars, for ten years.

content.content_text: The 93rd Academy Awards ceremony took place on April 25, 2021, two months later than usual because of the COVID-19 pandemic, and was held for the first time at Union Station in Los Angeles, with no official host. Nomadland (2021) won Best Picture, and Chloé Zhao became the second woman to win the Oscar for Best Director and the first woman of color to do so. At 83, Anthony Hopkins became the oldest actor to win a competitive acting Oscar, for The Father (2020), and Frances McDormand won her third Oscar for Best Actress. It was also the first edition with a single Sound category, which merged Sound Editing and Sound Mixing.

content.title: Reception
content.description: An estimated 23.6 million viewers watched the ceremony live, with a 5.3 rating among key demographic viewers. That was a 20% drop from the previous year's ceremony, making it the least-watched Oscars ceremony of all time. The ceremony was still ranked as the most-watched awards show of the 2019–2020 television season in the United States, since declining viewership has been observed across all awards shows in recent years. The 2020 Oscars were also one of the last live programs to air in the United States amid the current upheaval in the overall show schedule caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

information.contentTitle: Bong Joon Ho wins Best Director
information.contentText: When accepting the award for Best Director, Bong Joon-ho said through his interpreter: "When I was young and studying cinema, there was a saying that I carved deep into my heart, which is, 'The most personal is the most creative.'" He then said in English that the quote had come from "our great Martin Scorsese," which led the audience to give Scorsese an enthusiastic ovation. Bong later confirmed at a press conference with South Korean media that he had read the quote in a book written by David Thompson; Bong did not mention the book's title at the time, but it turned out to be Scorsese on Scorsese, co-written by Thompson and Ian Christie.

information.contentText: James Corden and Rebel Wilson presented the award for Best Visual Effects dressed in cat costumes to satirize their lead roles in Cats (a film heavily criticized for its visual effects, among other things) and told the audience: "As cast members of the motion picture Cats, nobody more than us understands the importance of good visual effects."; Mills said that Corden came up with the idea. content.title: Ceremony
content.description:
At its board meeting in April 2019, the Academy voted to rename the "Best Foreign Language Film" category to "Best International Feature Film." Animated films and documentaries would also qualify for the renamed award, but the remaining criteria would stay the same, requiring entries to have most of their dialogue in a language other than English. The Best Makeup and Hairstyling category was expanded from seven finalists and three nominees to ten finalists and five nominees.

On January 9, 2020, ABC Entertainment president Karey Burke revealed that, for the second year in a row, the ceremony would not have a host, citing the success of the format at the previous ceremony (when comedian Kevin Hart had stepped down from the role). Burke promised that the ceremony would showcase "big entertainment values, big musical numbers, comedy and star power."

information.contentTitle: Eminem - Lose Yourself Live at the 2020 Oscars
information.contentText: A highlight of the ceremony was Eminem's surprise performance of "Lose Yourself," from the film 8 Mile (2002). The song was nominated for and won Best Original Song in 2003, but Eminem declined to attend the ceremony because he lacked confidence that the song would actually win, among other factors. The idea of bringing Eminem back originated with Mills and the Academy, who wanted to keep a "high-energy" musical act in line with the opening performances by Justin Timberlake and Queen + Adam Lambert at the 2017 and 2019 editions, respectively, as well as to find a way to give Eminem the chance to perform his winning song. In addition, Eminem found the timing opportune, as he had just released a new album, Music to Be Murdered By. The performance was a closely guarded secret among the ceremony's producers, and Eminem would have the option of pulling out of the show if his involvement in the awards was discovered before it took place; his performance was therefore scheduled for the middle of the ceremony rather than as an opening act, so that if he backed out, it would not disrupt the program.

content.title: Host
content.description:
On December 4, 2018, it was announced that Kevin Hart would host the ceremony. At the time, Hart expressed how honored and excited he was by the invitation to host. Controversy began when old comments and jokes made by Hart surfaced containing slurs and homophobic language. After Hart refused to apologize on the matter, on December 6 he ruled out hosting the Oscars, saying he did not want to be a public "distraction" for the ceremony.

On January 9, 2019, it was reported that the Academy was planning to hold the ceremony without a host, choosing instead to invite a series of presenters for the various segments and the presentation of awards in the various categories. If this scenario materialized, it would be the first time the ceremony had no main host since the 1989 Oscars. Previous hosts such as Seth MacFarlane, Ellen DeGeneres, Neil Patrick Harris, Chris Rock and Jimmy Kimmel showed no interest in hosting the ceremony again. Finally, on February 5, 2019, the Academy announced, through a spokesperson and without giving further details, that the ceremony would not have a main host.

content.title: Categories presented during commercial breaks
content.description:
In order to shorten the ceremony's television broadcast, the Academy announced on February 11, 2019, that four categories (Best Cinematography, Best Live Action Short Film, Best Film Editing and Best Makeup and Hairstyling) would be presented during commercial breaks. However, the Oscar presentations in those categories would be streamed online through the official website, and the winners' speeches would be aired later in the ceremony. After some backlash, notably from some of the professionals nominated in those categories, the Academy reversed the decision four days later and announced that all 24 categories would be presented during the live broadcast of the ceremony.

This edition's television broadcast was expected to last three hours, with an estimated 90 seconds allotted to each winner (or winners) in the various categories, from the moment the names are announced until they take the stage and finish their acceptance speech. The ceremony's broadcast ended up lasting 3 hours and 23 minutes, the shortest since 2012.

content.title: Ceremony
content.description:
Despite mixed reviews of the previous ceremony, the Academy rehired Michael De Luca and Jennifer Todd to produce the event for the second year in a row. In May 2017, another decision mirroring that year's ceremony was announced: Jimmy Kimmel would host again. Kimmel said he was thrilled to helm the gala for another year: "Hosting the Oscars was a highlight of my career and I am grateful to Cheryl (Boone Isaacs), Dawn (Hudson) and the Academy for inviting me back to work with De Luca and Todd. If you thought we screwed up the ending of this year's show, wait until you see what we have planned for the 90th!" The host thus promoted the ceremony with an intense campaign of numerous commercials and interviews on his talk show, Jimmy Kimmel Live!.

On December 4, 2017, it was announced that the pre-show and opening monologue had been scheduled thirty minutes earlier than in previous broadcasts. In the first half of the nominations announcement, on January 23, 2018, the category presentations were pre-recorded by actresses Priyanka Chopra, Rosario Dawson, Gal Gadot, Salma Hayek, Michelle Rodriguez, Zoe Saldana, Molly Shannon, Rebel Wilson and Michelle Yeoh.

By awards tradition, the previous year's Best Actor winner usually presents the Oscar for Best Actress; on this occasion, however, Casey Affleck chose not to present because of sexual harassment allegations. In his place, Jodie Foster and Jennifer Lawrence took charge of the category. The Best Actor award was also presented by a female duo, instead of Emma Stone. Warren Beatty and Faye Dunaway were chosen to announce the Oscar for Best Picture, as a way of making amends for the previous ceremony's blunder.

content.title: Retrospective Assessment and Ratings
content.description:
The 2018 edition received mixed reviews from television and film critics. The main point of analysis was Jimmy Kimmel's moderate, restrained hosting. Hank Stuever, a journalist at The Washington Post, commented that "in his second year, Kimmel showed that the broadcast doesn't need to be anything other than crisp and confident, with an entertaining pace [...] we [viewers] have no pretension of making entertainment industry history, we just want to watch another Oscar night." David Edelstein, chief critic at New York Magazine, opined: "this was the best, most inspiring and most likable broadcast of the ceremony I have watched; but, on the other hand, it was also, in terms of the awards, one of the most disappointing." Richard Lawson of Vanity Fair noted that "as host, Kimmel struck a careful, meticulously calculated tone... Sunday night did an admirable job of acknowledging all the political turmoil surrounding it." CNN critic Brian Lowry said that "the Oscars are a big mess that clumsily tries to congratulate the truly deserving; however, if the intention was ultimately not to ignore the outside world and to serve society, Kimmel and the Academy did very well."

Other figures, on the other hand, gave the ceremony negative reviews. Television critic Maureen Ryan of Variety commented: "taking the show as a whole, I felt a more or less low vibe. Usually, two hours into the broadcast the numbing effect sets in, but despite host Kimmel's efforts, this edition was languid, lacking energy." James Poniewozik of The New York Times: "despite the recent upheaval in Hollywood, the ceremony largely focused on celebrating film." Columnist Kristi Turnquist of The Oregonian commented: "it was utterly respectful, a formal and dull kind of ceremony."

According to Nielsen Ratings, the ABC broadcast drew 26.5 million viewers in the United States, 19% fewer than the previous ceremony, making the 2018 edition the least-watched in Oscar history.
